_setup: Free developer account at developer.okta.com. Your domain is the one in the URL,
usually dev-NNNNNN.okta.com or integrator-NNNNN.okta.com.
THE ISSUER IS THE DECISION THAT MATTERS. Okta has two kinds of authorization server:
https://YOUR_DOMAIN                  the org server, for Okta's own management API
https://YOUR_DOMAIN/oauth2/default   a custom server, for your applications
They issue different tokens and support different grants. Use the second unless you
know you want the first.
1. Applications > Create App Integration > OIDC > Single-Page Application.
Sign-in redirect URI: http://localhost:3000/callback. Note the Client ID.
2. Applications > Create App Integration > API Services. That app type is what carries
the client_credentials grant. Note its Client ID and keep the secret for the shell.
3. Security > API > default > Access Policies. A free org ships a policy allowing every
client; if yours does not, add one for the API Services app or client_credentials is
refused with access_denied.
For the user flow, which needs a token without a browser:
4. Directory > People > Add person, with a password you set rather than an activation
email, and no forced password change on first sign in.
5. The user flow needs an app carrying the Resource Owner Password grant. A
Single-Page Application cannot: it is public, and that grant has no PKCE to stand in.
Create Applications > Create App Integration > OIDC > Web Application, tick
Resource Owner Password alongside Authorization Code, and use its credentials in
`user` below. Leave `user` out to run the unattended tier alone.
Then: export OKTA_SERVICE_SECRET=... OKTA_WEB_SECRET=... OKTA_TEST_PASSWORD=... \
&& node conformance/run.mjs okta
